title: Preserve robots.txt parser results for concurrent waiters
body:
## Motivation

With robots.txt obedience enabled, a disallowed URL is still downloaded when another request to the same host is already waiting on the first robots.txt lookup. The download succeeds and the page is passed to the spider.

Requests for one host all wait on a single Deferred stored in the per-host parser cache. robot_parser returned the value of awaiting that Deferred, and that await delivers the result to one callback, so every later waiter gets None and the middleware allows the download.

## What this changes

robot_parser still awaits the shared Deferred, then returns the parser already stored for that host, which is the parsed robots.txt or None if retrieval failed, and asserts the cache entry is no longer a Deferred. The two existing concurrent-request tests, on both reactors, now cover one allowed URL and two disallowed URLs and check that robots.txt is downloaded once. test_robotstxt_error_multiple_reqs and test_robotstxt_error_multiple_reqs_asyncio cover the same concurrency when the robots.txt download fails, with every waiter allowed through after that single attempt.

## How it was tested

Pytest -q tests/test_downloadermiddleware_robotstxt.py stopped while loading conftest and did not run any test.

Fixes #8297

title: Make DiskDupeFilter commit within JOBDIR_SYNC_EVERY
body:
`DiskDupeFilter` only committed its SQLite database on close, so a killed crawl lost every fingerprint and re-sent requests it had already seen. It now commits after every `JOBDIR_SYNC_EVERY` new fingerprints, like the scheduler does with `active.json`.

Part of #7978.

title: Order the Cookie header by path length, then creation time
body:
RFC 6265 §5.4 lists cookies of equal path length from oldest to newest, but `http.cookiejar` leaves ties in storage order, so a server that reads the first of two same-name cookies could get a different value than a browser would send. The cookie jar now records each cookie's creation order, kept when a cookie is replaced, and sorts by it.

Part of #5431.

title: Remove the dead UnicodeDammit test and assert the exact replacement in test_replace_wrong_encoding
body: Scrapy no longer uses UnicodeDammit, so the commented-out FIXME check was dead, and its expectation was wrong anyway: an undeclared body that is not valid UTF-8 gets an auto-detected encoding, not replacement characters. With an explicit `utf-8` encoding the decoded text is exactly `'PREFIX�SUFFIX'`, so the test now asserts that instead of only checking that the parts are present.

title: Fix robots.txt enforcement failing open for multiple concurrent waiters (#8297)
body:
Resolves #8297.

### Description
As reported and discussed in #8297, when multiple concurrent requests to the same host wait on the shared `robots.txt` Deferred during initial fetch/parsing, `RobotsTxtMiddleware.robot_parser()` previously did:
```python
parser = self._parsers[netloc]
if isinstance(parser, Deferred):
    return await maybe_deferred_to_future(parser)
return parser
```
Under Twisted, `Deferred.asFuture()` attaches callbacks to the Deferred that do not return the result (`maybeSucceed` returns `None`), consuming the result for subsequent callbacks in the chain. Consequently, the first waiter received the parsed `RobotParser`, but subsequent concurrent waiters received `None`. Because `process_request_2()` treats `None` as "no parser available", all subsequent concurrent waiters bypassed robots.txt enforcement and were allowed to fetch forbidden paths.

### Solution
- Chain a dedicated per-waiter `Deferred` using `parser.addCallbacks(cb, eb)` where `cb` explicitly returns `result` and forwards it to the per-waiter Deferred before conversion to future.
- Added regression tests in `tests/test_downloadermiddleware_robotstxt.py` for both Twisted Deferreds and asyncio covering 3+ concurrent requests to ensure disallowed paths are strictly rejected with `IgnoreRequest`.

- [x] I have read the [contributing guide](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/master/contributing.html) and [set up pre-commit](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/master/contributing.html#pre-commit).

title: Fix fail-open robots.txt enforcement for concurrent requests to same host
body:
## Description
Fixes #8297

When `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True`, multiple concurrent requests targeting the same host before `robots.txt` has finished downloading share a single Twisted `Deferred` instance inside `RobotsTxtMiddleware.robot_parser()`.

In #6802, `robot_parser` was refactored to an async coroutine that awaited `maybe_deferred_to_future(parser)`. Because Twisted's `Deferred.asFuture()` consumes the Deferred's result without returning it (`maybeSucceed` sets the future's result and returns `None`), only the first concurrent waiter received the parsed `RobotParser` instance. All subsequent concurrent waiters received `None`.

In `RobotsTxtMiddleware.process_request_2(rp, request)`, `rp is None` was treated as "no parser available -> allow request", causing all subsequent concurrent requests to silently fail open and bypass robots exclusion rules even for disallowed paths.

## Solution
1. Restore per-waiter `Deferred` instances in `RobotsTxtMiddleware.robot_parser()`.
2. Register callback and errback handlers that forward the parsed result (`RobotParser | None` or `Failure`) to each waiter's private `Deferred` while returning the result so subsequent callbacks in Twisted's callback chain receive it unchanged.
3. Await each waiter's private Deferred via `maybe_deferred_to_future(d)`. This preserves proper result delivery to all concurrent waiters and prevents cancellation of one waiter from canceling the shared robots.txt download.

## Tests Added
- `test_robotstxt_multiple_reqs_forbidden`: Regression test with `DeferredList` confirming multiple concurrent disallowed requests are rejected with `IgnoreRequest`.
- `test_robotstxt_multiple_reqs_asyncio_forbidden`: Reproduction test under `asyncio.gather`.
- `test_robotstxt_error_multiple_reqs`: Error path regression test when robots.txt fails to download.
- `test_robotstxt_subsequent_requests_cached_parser`: Verifies cached parser reuse after initial resolution.
- `test_robotstxt_multiple_hosts_concurrency`: Verifies multi-host concurrent isolation.
- `test_robotstxt_cancellation_isolation`: Verifies that canceling one waiter does not cancel the shared download.
- `test_robotstxt_concurrent_forbidden_stats`: Verifies stats counters and download deduplication.
- `TestRobotsTxtMiddlewareWithPythonRobotParser`: Verifies all behaviors against `PythonRobotParser` backend.

title: Fix robots.txt enforcement for concurrent requests to the same host
body:
Fixes #8297.

- [x] I have read the [contributing guide](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/master/contributing.html) and [set up pre-commit](https://docs.scrapy.org/en/master/contributing.html#pre-commit).

## What

In `RobotsTxtMiddleware.robot_parser()`, after awaiting the shared per-host `Deferred`, re-read the authoritative value from `self._parsers[netloc]` instead of using the awaited value:

```python
parser = self._parsers[netloc]
if isinstance(parser, Deferred):
    await maybe_deferred_to_future(parser)
    parser = self._parsers[netloc]
    assert not isinstance(parser, Deferred)
return parser
```

Two regression tests are added to `tests/test_downloadermiddleware_robotstxt.py`, covering the concurrent + disallowed combination (the existing concurrent tests only used allowed URLs).

## Why

All waiters for the same host share one `Deferred` (#6802 simplified this from per-waiter Deferreds), and its result is consumed by the first waiter:

- under the asyncio reactor, `maybe_deferred_to_future()` resolves to `Deferred.asFuture()` (`scrapy/utils/defer.py`), which hands the result to the first waiter and `None` to later ones;
- under the non-asyncio reactor, the raw `Deferred` is returned and later waiters receive `None` through the Twisted callback chain the same way.

`process_request_2()` treats `None` as "no parser available" and allows the request (`scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/robotstxt.py`), so with `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY=True` every same-host request after the first concurrent one silently bypasses robots.txt enforcement (fail-open).

Re-reading `self._parsers[netloc]` after the await is authoritative for every waiter, because both writers update the dict *before* firing the Deferred: `_parse_robots()` and `_robots_error()`. The error path keeps its existing semantics (parser `None` → request proceeds), so there is no behavior change beyond the bug fix. Root cause confirmed by @wRAR in #8297 (introduced by #6802).

Note: #8307 proposed the same minimal fix for the asyncio path but was auto-closed by the unattended-PR guard and is inactive. This PR additionally covers the non-asyncio reactor, where the same fail-open occurs and which was verified locally (below).

## How I verified

Environment: Python 3.13.12, Twisted 26.4.0, pytest 9.1.1, `pip install -e .` from this branch.

1. Reproduction script: 3 concurrent `process_request()` calls against a robots.txt that disallows `/admin/`, asserting `["ALLOWED", "IGNORED", "IGNORED"]`:
   - on master it fails under **both** `--reactor=asyncio` and `--reactor=default`: one of the disallowed requests comes back ALLOWED, e.g. `{'allowed': 'ALLOWED', 'admin/one': 'IGNORED', 'admin/two': 'ALLOWED'}`;
   - with this change it passes under both reactors.
2. `pytest tests/test_downloadermiddleware_robotstxt.py -q`:
   - master: `16 passed, 16 skipped`;
   - with this change: `18 passed, 18 skipped` (`--reactor=asyncio`, CI default) and `16 passed, 20 skipped` (`--reactor=default`, where the new `only_asyncio` tests are skipped and the new `DeferredList`-based test runs and passes).
3. The new tests fail without the fix and pass with it: `pytest tests/test_downloadermiddleware_robotstxt.py -q -k disallowed` → 2 failed on master (asyncio reactor; under `--reactor=default` the non-asyncio variant fails too), all pass with this change.
4. `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy scrapy/downloadermiddlewares/robotstxt.py` are clean; the full robotstxt suite was run 5 times per reactor with no flakes.

title: fix(robotstxt): deliver parsed parser to all concurrent waiters
body:
## Summary

Fixes #8297: concurrent requests to the same host could silently bypass `robots.txt` enforcement.

## Root cause

Concurrent same-host requests share a single Twisted `Deferred` for the robots.txt fetch/parse in `RobotsTxtMiddleware.robot_parser()`. Each waiter awaited it through `maybe_deferred_to_future()`, which calls `Deferred.asFuture()`.

Twisted's `asFuture()` *consumes* the Deferred's result (see its docstring: "converting a Deferred to a Future consumes both its result and its errors"). So only the **first** waiter received the parsed parser; every additional waiter received `None`. `process_request_2()` treats `None` as "no parser available", so those requests **failed open** and bypassed `ROBOTSTXT_OBEY`.

A minimal reproduction confirms the behavior — with three concurrent requests (one allowed, two disallowed), the second disallowed request returned `ALLOWED`:

```
ALLOWED  http://site.local/allowed
BLOCKED  http://site.local/private/a.html
ALLOWED  http://site.local/private/b.html   # wrong: should be BLOCKED
```

## Change

In `robot_parser()`, after awaiting the shared `Deferred`, read the final value back from `self._parsers[netloc]` instead of trusting the (consumed) `asFuture()` result:

```python
parser = self._parsers[netloc]
if isinstance(parser, Deferred):
    await maybe_deferred_to_future(parser)
    parser = self._parsers[netloc]
return parser
```

Every concurrent waiter now receives the actual `RobotParser` (or `None` on error), restoring correct allow/deny decisions.

## Tests

Added `test_robotstxt_multiple_reqs_asyncio_disallowed`, which races one allowed and two disallowed requests against the same host and asserts the disallowed ones are both blocked.

- Before the fix the test fails with `[False, True, False]`; after the fix it passes with `[False, True, True]`.
- Full `test_downloadermiddleware_robotstxt.py` suite: **17 passed, 17 skipped** (`--reactor asyncio`).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files.
